title_en: Mystery Thriller Series Yaga Gets Renewed for Season 2, Carrie-Anne Moss to Return
summary_en: Canadian streaming service Crave has greenlit the mystery thriller series Yaga for a second season, with Carrie-Anne Moss confirmed to return.
body_en:
Canadian streaming service Crave has greenlit the mystery thriller series Yaga for a second season, with Carrie-Anne Moss confirmed to return. The decision comes prior to Season 1's two-episode finale on November 27.
Yaga debuted on October 23 and quickly became #1 on Crave. It also took the top spot for "exclusive series launch ever" on AMC+ in the U.S., along with holding the #1 position in multiple other countries around the world.
“The incredible response to Yaga has blown us away,” Justin Stockman, Vice President, Global Content, Bell Media said in a press release. “Congratulations to Kat Sandler and our production partners at Blink49 Studios and Front Street Pictures. Together, we’ve created a bold and daring Canadian series that we believe strongly in, and we can’t wait to see where Season 2 takes us.”
Pancho Mansfield, President of Global Scripted, Blink49 Studios, added, “Kat Sandler has brought such a bold and distinctive vision to Yaga, and we’re incredibly proud to have supported her in bringing it to the screen. To see her first television series as creator and showrunner resonate with audiences in Canada and around the world has been enormously rewarding. We’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Bell Media to bring the next chapter of Yaga to life.”
For those unfamiliar, Yaga is a modern retelling of the European folklore around Baba Yaga – a witch who takes on the role of both villain and mentor, harnessing both good and evil depending on the story. The new series is from Kat Sandler, who created a stage play of the same name and serves as writer, showrunner, and executive producer.
In our first two-episode review, we gave it an 8 saying, "Yaga evokes a kind of weirdness combined with a sultry, thriller mystery that sucks you right into the story. The show makes you feel like you’re a detective right alongside the main characters, trying to solve the case and pick up on all the strange and otherworldly clues along the way, while sitting on the edge of your seat waiting for the next episode to drop."
For more on Yaga, read what Sandler had to say about being inspired by Dexter and Hannibal, while also calling Baba Yaga the "OG bad girl of fairytales," in our exclusive interview from San Diego Comic-Con.
Jessie Wade is Associate Director of Editorial Programming at IGN. You can find her watching the latest drama and fantasy shows, as well as getting lost in too many books. She's also low-key obsessed with cheesy rom-coms. In terms of gaming, you can find her playing the latest Pokemon, cozy indies, and Elder Scrolls Online.
